6,560 likes, 27 comments - ishitamangal on October 4, 2026: "45 days ago, I was doing 10K in 1 hour 25 minutes. Today I did it in 1 hour🥹🏃‍♀️⚡ Training 5–6 days a week under the guidance of my coach has helped me get here much faster than I ever expected. Forever grateful to @neilsingh09 for giving me the best training pattern and to @manveindrasingh for basically forcing me to sign up for every race possible 😂🤝

Ran the Sekhon India Air Force 10K Race today ✈️🇮🇳 The race goodies and arrangements were absolutely top notch. The only struggle was the number of people walking right in front of us at the start, which made it difficult to find a clear passage and build pace initially. But every race teaches me something new mostly that my body is capable of doing things my brain had already declared impossible 😂 This one was AMAZING. Another race in 2 weeks. Watch out. 👀🔥🏃‍♀️ @sekhoniafmarathon 

#10KRun #RunningJourney #RaceDay #WomenWhoRun #RunnerLife".

90s frosty lips feel like a flashback in one swipe. No? That icy shimmer instantly takes us back to a time when makeup was bold, playful, and unapologetic. Think mall lights, pop icons, glossy magazines, and that cool girl confidence. It was never about being subtle, it was about being seen. Now it is trending back because nostalgia is having a moment and the 90s knew how to have fun with beauty. The frost is back with smoother formulas and a modern glow, but the attitude remains cool, confident, and dramatic.

posts.meta_description:
28K likes, 542 comments - ishitamangal on August 4, 2025: "I’m embracing the way sarees were once worn in the golden age of India - without a blouse. ⚠️ In those times, draping was all about fluidity, freedom, and the natural elegance of the female form. The saree itself was the statement. It didn’t need an extra layer to prove its sophistication. It was only after colonization, when Victorian ideals crept into our culture, that covering up became the norm and the blouse was stitched into the Indian woman’s wardrobe. What was once effortless grace slowly became “proper dressing,” rewriting centuries of our fashion history.

Today I chose to dress like an apsara blouseless. Embracing the saree as approved by our ancestors. Do you approve of this look in 2025? 👼🏻 

Hosted by @thewordmagazine 
Saree and jewels by @anumerton 
Drape inspired by @natasha.thasan 
Styled by @sal.did.a.thing 
Hair by @makeupandhairby_sonalii 
Makeup by me 💁🏻‍♀️
Social media manager by @ursnana_ 

#IshitaMangal #Apsara #BlouselessSaree #SareeCulture #WhiteSaree #IndianAdornment #IndianCulture #IndiaTradions #AncientIndia".

posts.meta_description:
22K likes, 1,193 comments - ishitamangal on February 12, 2026: "Comment “IMLIPS” to get a link of all products 

I’m always testing lip colours because brown skin doesn’t get the luxury of “any shade will do.” Some colours turn grey. Some go neon. Some look stunning in the tube and completely disappear on melanin. So when I find lip shades that actually work, I want to show them to you. 

These lip colours are brown skin friendly because the undertones are right, the pigment is balanced, and the formulas don’t fight your natural lip colour. They don’t need fixing with liner. They don’t wash you out. They just sit well on brown skin.

And good formulas matter. If a lipstick is cracking, drying, or vanishing in two hours, the shade doesn’t matter. These feel comfortable, wear well, and look good in real life not just under studio lights.

This isn’t about hyping products. It’s about saving brown girls from trial and error fatigue. Inmein se koi shade tum par weird nahi lagega. This is my #IMSold waada to you! Enjoy! 👄 

#makeuptutorial #makeupgirl #lipsticks".

posts.meta_description:
178K likes, 1,044 comments - ishitamangal on February 7, 2026: "I was watching old Bollywood films and couldn’t stop noticing the hair. Women like Kajol and Madhuri Dixit had volume, texture, flyaways. Their hair moved when they moved. It looked like it had life in it. It looked real. 

Back then, that was just normal hair.
Today, the same hair would be called messy or “not done.” I know trends change. But I really miss when hair didn’t need control, heat, and perfection to be considered pretty. Sure even I enjoy my hair be styled and groomed but I would not like to be judged for the times that it’s not. 

Do you miss seeing real hair on screen and in reality too? 👀💭

Use hashtag #IMMyHair and tag me with your natural hair 💁🏻‍♀️

My jewelry is from @shilpigoyaljewellery 

(hair rant, talking about hair, hair thoughts, beauty talk, real vs processed hair) 
#HairTalk #RealHair HairTexture #UnprocessedHair Processedhair".
